methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $8.6B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 6 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in AI & Software. Range: $3.8B - $39.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Wayve, a Series D AI & Software company founded by Amar Shah and Alex Kendall, is evaluated against a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Palantir). The peer set spans autonomous systems and frontier AI, including Figure AI ($39.0B Series C), Skild AI ($14.0B Series C), and Crusoe Energy ($10.0B Series C), with valuations ranging from $3.8B to $39.0B.

Two valuation methods triangulate the assessment. The Stage-Progression method applies a typical 1.5x step-up multiplier to Wayve's last post-money valuation of $8.6B, implying $12.9B. The Peer-Median approach anchors to the median valuation of six same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables at $9.2B. The peer cohort exhibits wide dispersion—Figure AI's $39.0B outlier reflects investor appetite for robotics-adjacent AI, while SandboxAQ at $5.8B (Series E) suggests valuation compression at later stages.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $7.8B to $14.8B, with a median of $11.0B. Wayve's current $8.6B valuation sits near the lower bound, consistent with Series D positioning but 19% below the median. Key uncertainties include the sustainability of outlier peer valuations (particularly Figure AI) and whether Wayve's technology differentiation justifies a premium to peer medians given deployment risk and competitive intensity in autonomous systems.
